source: The public copy of the seats file of the house (seat, title, holder, areas, and bundle), plus the machinery and the gates of each seat, listed by hand until a bundle manifest exists. The local cockpit is planned to read the private file; this page renders the public copy. No private field.

where.site gate: runs in the deploy gate of this site on every push to main; a failing check keeps the previous build live
where.module repository: runs in the continuous integration of the CTO powersuit repository on every change
where.pre-push: runs on the holder's machine before every push, with data that never leaves it
where.module: ships with the named module and runs in the deploy gate of a repository that has fitted it; this site's gate does not run it
where.policy: a rule the holder follows by hand; its enforcement is an open item where one is named

machinery.name: direction
machinery.what: A weekly review that reads the tracker across all areas and writes the memo: what moved, what is blocked, the allocation of the week, and the decisions needed. A confirmed decision becomes a tracker item.

machinery.name: decisions
machinery.what: Requests for comments, numbered decision records with supersede links, and a review of the decision log.

machinery.name: cockpit
machinery.what: The queue of items that wait on the holder, one scorecard per area, and the trend: 14 days on the public cockpit, 12 weeks on the local one.

gates.what: Every review memo names its date and period, carries the four sections, and gives every decision a status.
Every decision record has a status, an owner, and a date. The decision records of this site live in its docs tree.

machinery.name: sdlc
machinery.what: The lifecycle of a change: tickets, a change review on every pull request, a test strategy, and a release with a rollback plan.

machinery.name: gate
machinery.what: The deploy gate: rules with pass and fail fixtures, run records, and a deploy job that waits for the gate.

machinery.name: docs
machinery.what: Pages with an owner and review dates, runbooks, a sweep for stale pages, and a health page that lists the pages past review.

machinery.name: observability and reliability
machinery.what: Dashboards as code, alert routes, availability targets per service, a status page, incidents, and postmortems.

machinery.name: security and compliance
machinery.what: Workflow steps pinned to a commit and limited to an owner allowlist, a secrets scan, an access review, threat models, a quarantine for third-party text, a control map by clause number, and the legal baseline of a site.

machinery.name: ai-ops and red-team
machinery.what: A shared harness for coding agents with narrow permissions, spend metered per request, a coordinator pattern, and pressure tests with a known right answer.

gates.what: Every workflow step from outside the repository is pinned to a full commit.
Every workflow step comes from an owner on the allowlist.
The deploy job waits for the gate; a failing check keeps the previous build live.
Every gate check of every module passes its pass fixture and fails its fail fixture.
Every changed module raises its version, and the changelog names the release.
Every change names a ticket or a decision. On this site, the pull request title carries the issue or the decision.
Every page of the docs tree carries an owner and review dates; the health page lists the pages past review. A gate check on the fields is an open decision (issue 27).
No secret pattern in a tracked file.
Every service has an owner, an availability target, and a runbook.
Every alert rule names a route and a runbook.
The security contact file exists and has not expired. This site has none yet (issue 12).
No page loads a file from a third party (decision record ADR-0010 of this site). The module's check is not in this site's gate.
The shared agent settings carry no secret and no wildcard permission.
Every pressure-test run names the expected and the observed decision.

machinery.name: finops
machinery.what: A cost baseline from invoices and billing exports, showback per team or service, unit costs, an audit of the tool stack, and a cost export in one open format.

machinery.name: FinOps space
machinery.what: The public cost pages of the platform, each figure with its period and its source.

gates.what: Every cost figure on a page carries a date range and a source. The cost pages of this site follow the rule by hand.

machinery.name: hiring
machinery.what: An interview loop in which each stage collects one signal, rubrics with anchored levels, debriefs with evidence before votes, and the profile of the next platform owner.

machinery.name: handover
machinery.what: Training checklists per module, exit criteria, and a test plan that shows the new owner runs the platform from the docs alone.

gates.what: Every rubric dimension has anchored levels.
Every installed module has a named owner.

machinery.name: aieo
machinery.what: A plain index for agents, structured data that matches the visible page, a fixed query set probed against AI search engines, and predictions hashed before a page goes live.

machinery.name: site gate
machinery.what: The conformity gate on every page of the house's sites, with its history in the open.

machinery.name: change review
machinery.what: An advisory review of every pull request by the coding agent, with the pull request as files, no shell, and no network: in the pipeline once it has its key, from the holder's machine until then.

machinery.name: editorial standards
machinery.what: The standards on this page: sources and verification, the gates every piece passes, and how corrections are made.

gates.what: No service closer, filler idiom, or stage hook in the copy of any page.
No placeholder text on any page.
A canonical link on every page, root-absolute links only, and every page in the sitemap.
Every prediction file matches its recorded hash.
A push that adds a private term stops on the holder's machine; the site gate runs the same check as a dry run only, with the list kept off the repository (issue 63).
The holder approves and merges every change; an agent session never merges on its own. Denying the merge path to agent sessions is an open item (issue 51).

machinery.name: vault
machinery.what: A plain-Markdown knowledge base with keyword and semantic search served to the coding agent, seeded from an interview, and fed by a skill that turns documents into linked one-idea notes.

machinery.name: quarantine
machinery.what: Third-party text goes into a store outside every indexed folder; a local model with no tools returns a summary and never the raw text.

machinery.name: library
machinery.what: The catalog of files and works in the local cockpit, rescanned on demand.

machinery.name: docs review sweep
machinery.what: Stale pages found, checked against the system they describe, and dated again only after that check.

gates.what: Private folders and notes are never indexed, never returned, and refused on read.
The pages imported from the knowledge base carry at least one date, and the newest is within 90 days; the gate reports the result and does not block on it.
